1. The theatre assigns haze canisters through a Reformat. Deliver a booked cue to port 0 and a declined cue to port 1, in the order that the stage manager submits them. The dictionary records whether reservation_live permits bookings, bookings_used counts booked cues, and litres_drawn measures their combined fluid demand.

2. A suspended service produces SUSPENDED regardless of the contents of fluid_ml. While service is available, courtesy=true authorises a dry demonstration with no fluid demand. A false or absent courtesy requires fluid_ml to contain one to three digits, optionally a point and one or two decimal digits. Reject absent, empty, signed, spaced or otherwise damaged orders as BAD_ORDER.

3. For an ordinary cue, the decimal quantity is its demand. The allowance is 6.00 litres and four bookings; a prospective overrun produces OVERDRAWN. An exact fit is BOOKED. Every booking occupies one appointment, including a dry demonstration. At either allowance, further bookings are suspended. Declines change none of the shared entries.

4. Both audit destinations retain all source columns. litres_booked displays litres_drawn to two decimal places, such as 2.50; bookings_used shows the committed booking count and booking_result contains BOOKED, SUSPENDED, BAD_ORDER or OVERDRAWN. These figures describe the ledger after the current cue. A date-only cue_time denotes midnight UTC. programme_note has no operational role.

Supplied dictionary configuration: reservation_live=true; bookings_used=0; litres_drawn="0.00".

1. Route butterfly-house feeder tickets with a Partition: allocations go to port 0, measurement or allowance refusals to port 1, and tickets received while feeding is shut to port 2. Arrival sequence is the allocation order. Shared dictionary feeding_open is the boolean service permission; allocations_done is the long number issued; syrup_issued is the decimal syrup charged.

2. Education visits identified by education_visit=true incur no syrup charge and need no measurement. Otherwise syrup_ml must be an entire unsigned decimal, one to three integer digits with an optional point followed by one or two digits. Null approval is ordinary work. Null text, blanks, spaces and signs are BAD_MEASURE. Subtract sponsor_credit from an ordinary measurement, treating its null as zero; charge the greater of that difference and zero.

3. Admit a ticket as ALLOCATED when the charge fits within 6.00 total and fewer than four allocations have been made. A non-fitting ticket is EXHAUSTED. Increase the shared totals only for allocations, then shut feeding at six units or four tickets. feeding_open=false takes precedence over all measurement checks and gives SHUT; a refused request cannot reopen feeding.

4. All three destinations carry the unaltered source record, including observation_note, which is irrelevant to allocation. Log one info message per ticket containing ALLOCATED, SHUT, BAD_MEASURE or EXHAUSTED. Interpret placement_time without a time as UTC midnight. keeper_signature and sponsor_credit may remain null in the routed evidence.

Supplied dictionary configuration: feeding_open=true; allocations_done=0; syrup_issued="0.00".

1. The print room needs a two-port Reformat for letterpress pigment draws. A cleared docket reaches port 0; every other docket reaches port 1. Evaluate dockets in delivery order. Dictionary press_released is boolean permission to draw, pulls_authorised is a long count, and pigment_consumed is decimal consumption available to the next production stage.

2. A locked press returns LOCKED before investigating a docket. On a released press, a true proof_sheet means a dry proof and consumes nothing. Null proof_sheet means an inked pull. For an inked pull, pigment_ml accepts precisely one through three digits with an optional decimal point and one or two following digits. Empty, absent, signed or padded text gives BAD_DOCKET.

3. Multiply the parsed amount by density_factor, or by one when that factor is null. A proof consumes zero regardless of factor. The cumulative capacity is 6.00 and the authorised-pull allowance is four. Refuse an overrun as CAPACITY; equality fits. Each CLEARED docket adds consumption and one pull, even when consumption is zero. Lock the press when either allowance is reached. Other outcomes leave its dictionary untouched.

4. Copy all input columns onto the selected audit. pigment_consumed is the resulting decimal ledger rendered with two fractional digits, for example 1.25. pulls_authorised reports the resulting count and pull_result names CLEARED, LOCKED, BAD_DOCKET or CAPACITY. pull_time supplied as a date means UTC midnight. docket_annotation is retained for paperwork only.

Supplied dictionary configuration: press_released=true; pulls_authorised=0; pigment_consumed="0.00".

A PERMITTED ticket commits demand and one permit. At six consumed units or four permits coating becomes unavailable, with no subsequent reopening.

4. Never charge or count a refused ticket. Routing retains each source value, including nullable finish_description and retail_value. workshop_comment is unused. Write an info log message identifying each ticket outcome as PERMITTED, FINISHED, BAD_VOLUME or TOO_LARGE. A date-only dip_time is the UTC start of the stated day.

Mirror coating work orders

An observatory needs a Normalizer ledger for mirror coatings. Orders arrive together by mirror_serial, in event order; mirror serials are nonnegative. A different serial represents an independent coating account. KEEP commissions a prescription and REMOVE withdraws it. A withdrawal does not read reflectance_card. A later commissioning after withdrawal is a new installation.

Check workday_spelling as a complete yyyy-MM-dd calendar date, without surrounding spaces, interpreted as midnight UTC. KEEP also needs reflectance_card, trimmed, with an optional minus sign, one to six ASCII integer digits and an optional decimal point followed by one or two digits. Any failed check or unknown work_order produces INVALID, defect_note INPUT, and leaves the usable coating account untouched.

For a usable KEEP, compare the exact reflectance with the preceding usable KEEP for this serial, including one that produced UNCHANGED. Compare coating_alloy with the installed alloy after trimming and uppercasing; absent alloy agrees with blank. A difference in either comparison replaces the coating. Keep raw alloy spelling in the ledger. Replacement writes CLOSE before OPEN; the former describes the installed coating, never the equivalent intervening proposal. A commissioning with no coating in service writes OPEN. An equivalent order writes UNCHANGED. REMOVE writes CLOSE then RETIRED when in service, otherwise INACTIVE.

OPEN gets one long coating_keys number, starting 8001 with increment 1, as coating_revision; it stores exact reflectance_pct and coating_start. CLOSE reuses that revision and payload with coating_end equal to the withdrawal/replacement day; OPEN ends at null. Other events have null revision, reflectance, alloy and endpoints. Every row copies mirror_serial and docket_ref, sets ledger_event, and supplies accounting_month as UTC yyyy-MM, for example 2026-01, or empty if its day is invalid. defect_note is empty except on INVALID. Port 0 retains event order. inspection_ts, spare_budget, courier_note and line_no have no decision role.

Fountain commissioning register

Build a Normalizer for the parks fountain commissioning register. Each consecutive fountain_no block is a separate installation account, with no imported target rows. Fountain numbers are nonnegative. Source order within a block is authoritative.

The commissioning pressure is anchored to the first usable KEEP following the start of that account or a REMOVE. Even if later work replaces the nozzle, that commissioning pressure remains the numerical reference until withdrawal. A pressure difference of at least 2.00 bar from it warrants replacement. nozzle_stamp can also warrant replacement: compare its trimmed spelling, preserving letter case, with absent and blank equivalent. Installed rows retain the submitted stamp untrimmed. Equivalent orders are silent.

KEEP reads trimmed pressure_entry: allow a minus sign, one through six ASCII digits, and optionally a dot with one or two further digits. Both directives require activation_day spelled exactly yyyy-MM-dd and valid in the UTC calendar. REMOVE ignores pressure_entry. An unknown directive, malformed pressure on KEEP, or invalid date yields INVALID with rejection_code INPUT; such paperwork does not alter the usable installation account.

Port 0 carries register_kind OPEN for installation, CLOSE followed by OPEN for replacement, CLOSE alone for active withdrawal, and INACTIVE for a withdrawal with nothing installed. Recommissioning after withdrawal creates OPEN. Long sequence nozzle_keys starts at 8001, increment 1; only OPEN receives a fresh nozzle_revision. For OPEN record pressure_bar, raw nozzle_stamp and live_since, leaving live_until null. A CLOSE must reproduce the old revision, pressure, stamp and starting date, ending at the current activation day. INVALID and INACTIVE contain null installation payload. Copy fountain_no and permit_scan onto each event. permit_month is the valid UTC day formatted yyyy-MM, such as 2026-02, otherwise empty; rejection_code is otherwise empty. estimate_cost, crew_arrival, service_comment and visit_order are unused.

user:
Cabinet humidity publishing queues

Conservators publish humidity changes through a two-output Reformat. Cabinet accounts arrive in consecutive case_number blocks with nonnegative numbers. There are no target prescriptions to load. Each cabinet begins operating when its first usable KEEP arrives and may operate again after withdrawal.

Output 0 is the closure queue; output 1 is the new-prescription and paperwork queue. KEEP that differs from the installed humidity by strictly more than 2.00 creates a closure plus an opening. Exactly 2.00 does not qualify numerically. A lining_description difference also qualifies: null and empty agree, but every other raw character is significant. Compare against the last OPEN, not the preceding submission. Equivalent proposals create UNCHANGED on output 1. REMOVE creates CLOSE on output 0 if operating, or INACTIVE on output 1 otherwise; no additional retirement notice is required.

Require change_day to be an exact yyyy-MM-dd UTC calendar day. For KEEP, trim humidity_slip and accept optional minus, one to six ASCII digits, optionally followed by a point and one or two fractional digits. REMOVE does not inspect that slip. Bad dates, bad KEEP quantities and unknown instruction produce INVALID on output 1, form_problem INPUT, without altering the cabinet prescription.

Every OPEN takes one long humidity_keys identifier starting 8001, step 1, into humidity_revision. Its humidity_target is the parsed decimal, lining_description the raw source, coverage_begin the change day, and coverage_end null. CLOSE carries the old installed revision, target, lining and coverage_begin; coverage_end is the UTC calendar day immediately before change_day. UNCHANGED, INACTIVE and INVALID have those five payload fields null. All notices copy case_number and conservation_ticket, identify notice_class and carry filing_month in yyyy-MM, for example 2026-01; invalid dates give an empty month. form_problem is empty apart from INVALID. The four provenance columns contingency, survey_time, installer_remark and position_no do not affect publication.

user:
Heliostat focus classes

The solar field needs a Normalizer that records changes of optical class rather than every measurement. Receive each heliostat_number as one consecutive block of ordered events; heliostat numbers are nonnegative. KEEP proposes focal distance and surface finish, while REMOVE withdraws the prescription. Reinstallation is allowed.

A numerical class is the focal distance rounded to a whole decimal with halves away from zero. Compare a usable KEEP with the preceding usable KEEP, even when that earlier measurement needed no installation. Different classes trigger replacement. Independently, compare surface_finish exactly as nullable raw text: null differs from empty and spaces matter. Replacement is needed if either comparison differs. An equivalent KEEP becomes UNCHANGED without modifying the installed payload.

The event day effective_sheet_day must match ten-character yyyy-MM-dd and a possible UTC calendar date. Trim focal_distance_note for KEEP, allowing an optional minus, one to six ASCII integer digits and an optional dot with one or two fraction digits. REMOVE disregards distance text. Any invalid requirement or unrecognised movement yields INVALID and paperwork_code INPUT, retaining the existing usable optical account.

Send OPEN for a first installation, CLOSE then OPEN for replacement, CLOSE then RETIRED for withdrawal in service, and INACTIVE for withdrawal otherwise. Every emitted row copies heliostat_number and field_ticket, fills focus_event, and gives solar_month as the event's UTC yyyy-MM month, e.g. 2026-03, or empty for an invalid date. Other paperwork_code values are empty. Sequence optics_keys supplies long optical_revision values from 8001 by 1 only when OPEN is emitted. OPEN stores unrounded focal_distance, raw surface_finish and installed_on with removed_on null. CLOSE preserves the installed revision, distance, finish and installed_on, ending on this event's day. Audit events have all five installation fields null. reserve_cost, measurement_time, technician_message and row_number are irrelevant to these decisions.

Reef circulation prescriptions

A reef laboratory distinguishes reverse circulation from forward circulation in nursery_bay accounts. Each bay's requests are consecutive; bay numbers are nonnegative. Implement the prescription feed as a Normalizer, retaining source event order on its only output.

For this laboratory, negative circulation is one class and nonnegative circulation another. The class of the first successful KEEP of an installation cycle governs subsequent comparisons until REMOVE, even if replacement pumps were installed in between. mesh_grade is an additional independent replacement criterion; trim it and ignore case, with null equivalent to whitespace. Preserve its original spelling in installed records. Comparing within the same class and grade creates UNCHANGED. A changed class or grade creates CLOSE followed by OPEN.

request_type KEEP requires a circulation_reading that, after trim, has optional minus, one to six ASCII integer digits and at most two fractional digits after an optional dot. REMOVE ignores the reading. service_day is mandatory for either request and must be exactly yyyy-MM-dd with a real UTC calendar day. Unknown requests and defective paperwork produce one INVALID, repair_code INPUT. They cannot change which pump prescription is usable.

An installation with nothing currently enabled emits OPEN. REMOVE emits CLOSE only when enabled and otherwise emits nothing; a later KEEP starts a new installation cycle. OPEN alone draws a long pump_keys value (8001, increment 1) into pump_revision. Its circulation_rate, raw mesh_grade and enabled_day describe the proposal; disabled_day is null. A CLOSE retains the installed revision, rate, mesh and enabled_day, ending at service_day. Audit payload fields are null. Set circulation_event and copy nursery_bay and dive_record to every row. restoration_month contains the valid event month in UTC yyyy-MM form, for example 2026-01, or empty when invalid. repair_code is empty for all other events. grant_amount, diver_checkin, reef_comment and sampling_order have no operational effect.

A ceramics laboratory needs a Normalizer that evaluates individual pigment corrections from each glaze card. pigment_corrections is a comma-separated list. Null or empty parent text represents one invalid correction. Batch numbers are nonnegative and pigment amounts can be 0.

Other spelling contributes NUMBER and null pigment_amount; usable spelling gives the exact decimal. mixing_day must be exactly yyyy-MM-dd and a possible UTC day, else DATE. recipe_mark must be two uppercase ASCII letters and two ASCII digits, else CODE. Theatre counterweight child inspection

The theatre workshop supplies comma-separated counterweight readings to a Normalizer. Expand counterweight_cards in order and publish every child decision on port 0. Null or empty parent text supplies one invalid child. Commas preserve leading and interior zero-length readings, but trailing zero-length readings are omitted; a source consisting entirely of commas produces no readings. Copy all parent fields, use child_position as a zero-based index, and retain the parsed counterweight_mass even if another check rejects the child. Rigging positions are nonnegative; zero mass is allowed.

A child, after trim, accepts unsigned one-to-four ASCII integer digits with an optional dot and one or two fraction digits. Otherwise NUMBER applies and its parsed mass is null. inspection_day must be a real UTC calendar date written exactly yyyy-MM-dd, or DATE applies. hanger_mark is exactly two uppercase ASCII letters followed by two digits, otherwise CODE. An absent or negative operating_limit gives CAP.

A usable mass may be at most 110 percent of a usable operating_limit, using exact decimal arithmetic; exceeding that gives LIMIT. The duplicate tuple is rigging_position, exact mass, raw hanger_mark and raw inspection_day, compared with the most recently accepted child anywhere in the stream. Same values on another day are distinct. Parsed matching tuples give DUP even with CAP faults. Rejecting a child cannot change which tuple later siblings compare with.

The hatchery imports aeration-stone worksheets through a Normalizer. bubble_cards contains comma-separated readings. The manuscript laboratory bills ink stabilisation only on open laboratory dates. Implement a Reformat that returns one port 0 decision for every folio, maintaining input order.

An open date is Monday through Friday in UTC, excluding 2026-03-30, 2026-04-01, 2026-12-31 and 2027-01-01. Other dates produce CLOSED with null posted_charge and charge_difference, and charge_faults zero; dilution_entry and ink_charge are irrelevant on those dates.

On an open date, dilution_entry is an optional factor for ink_charge. Null, empty and whitespace-only content means one. Otherwise trim it and require an optional minus, one to six ASCII digits and an optional fractional part of one to three digits. Bad syntax yields TEXT, even with null ink_charge. An acceptable factor with null ink_charge yields MISSING. Otherwise decision_type is VALID and posted_charge is the exact product rounded to cents, ties away from zero. TEXT and MISSING have null posted_charge and charge_faults one. VALID has charge_faults zero. charge_difference remains null, and folios_seen is always one.

week_sunday is the Sunday starting the source UTC week, yyyy-MM-dd, for example 2026-03-29. A date-only treated_dt is midnight UTC. Copy manuscript_volume, folio_tag, treated_dt, conservator_name, shelf_reference, treatment_order and ink_note unchanged, including nulls. shelf_reference is opaque context. treatment_signed and area_weight have no effect on opening dates or charges.

compound_factor adjusts surface_charge. A missing, empty or whitespace-only factor equals one.
